name: Cummins India Ltd
title: Cummins India Ltd - 500480 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 sales up 18% to INR3,375 crore on data-centre gensets, but PBT fell 0.7% as commodity inflation squeezes margins; utilisation only 70–75% and capex kept in line with past years, so supply discipline is not the story.

summary.headline: Cummins India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR3,375 crore, but pre-exceptional PBT fell 0.7% to INR721 crore as commodity inflation hit margins.
summary.overview: Net sales hit a record INR3,375 crore, up 18% YoY and 14% QoQ, led by domestic sales of INR2,854 crore (+22% YoY). Exports were flat YoY at INR521 crore, with high-horsepower exports up 16% but low-horsepower exports down 20%. Profit before tax before exceptional items was INR721 crore, marginally lower YoY, as steel, pig iron, aluminium and copper inflation, freight and West Asia disruption weighed on margins. Management took one price increase at the start of Q2 FY27 and said it had not yet been absorbed by the market; no price hike was taken in Q1. Data centres drove a large share of power generation growth.

financial_highlights.metric: Profit before tax before exceptional items

segments.name: Power generation (domestic)
segments.commentary: INR1,424 crore, +35% YoY. Data centres were about 40% of power gen revenue in Q1 FY27 versus 23% in Q1 FY26. Split by range: LHP INR77 crore, MHP INR248 crore, HD INR125 crore, with HHP the remainder.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: INR886 crore, +14% YoY and +16% QoQ, slowing from a 20%-plus five-year CAGR. Management said the slowdown reflects a higher base, parts availability and supply disruption, and reiterated 20% growth potential.

segments.name: Industrial (domestic)
segments.commentary: INR458 crore, +10% YoY. Construction INR148 crore (flat YoY), rail INR145 crore (strong order book), compressor INR52 crore, marine INR50 crore; mining, defence and others the remainder.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: INR521 crore, flat YoY. HHP INR296 crore (+16% YoY), LHP INR180 crore (-20% YoY). Middle East weak due to West Asia crisis; Europe and Asia Pacific were the main growth markets.

guidance_outlook: Management expects strong demand in end markets to sustain, with inflation and supply chain constraints likely to continue through the year.
Will not give a gross margin target; says margins can improve from here but cannot say whether they will return to historic highs of about 36-37%.
One price increase taken at the start of Q2 FY27; further increases will depend on market absorption and cost recovery is not expected to be full.
Employee cost of about INR2,300 crore is a higher base for the remaining quarters, per management's confirmation.
Related-party export approvals are for the current fiscal year only and are a governance measure, not a signal of an existing UK order book.
Royalty rates standardised at 4% from a previous 1% to 8% range, which explains the higher royalty ratio.
capex_capacity: Capex is in line with the last few years and goes into existing plants; utilisation is 70-75% and rising.
High-HP genset capacity is tight across the industry; demand is outpacing capacity additions, and some orders may be lost on relationships and preference, not only supply.
No plans yet to build domestic capacity for QSK78 or QSK95; India data-centre volume is still mainly QSK60, with growing interest in QSK78 and QSK95.
BESS demonstrator installed at the Phaltan rebuild centre; management says it is close to first orders but has none yet.
demand_pricing: Power gen: strong order velocity across data centres, manufacturing, residential, commercial and realty; data-centre customers asked for earlier deliveries rather than deferrals.

Pricing: commodity costs (steel, pig iron, aluminium, copper), freight and supplier labour shortages drove the cost pressure; one price hike was taken at the start of Q2 and its market acceptance is unknown.
Data-centre pricing is order-by-order; lead time and site readiness matter more to customers than price.
Rail demand is strong (power cars, diesel-electric tower cars, hotel load converters); mining tenders are recovering; construction is flat with no new national highway tenders; marine is lumpy.
Exports: Middle East orders are not coming through as expected; Europe and Asia Pacific are growing. Management would not split exports by end segment.
Competition in power gen is intense, with more than 10-12 competitors cited.

qa_highlights.question: Are capacity constraints causing lost orders in QSK60/QSK95, and have lead times lengthened?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is outpacing supply for all high-HP players; capacity is being added at specific nodes. Management said order losses depend on customer relationships and preferences as well as supply.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margins return to the historical 36-37% from Q2 after price action?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commodity increases are unprecedented and it could not say whether margins would hit historic highs. It expects margins to improve as cost management gets better.

qa_highlights.question: Is the related-party export approval linked to an existing UK subsidiary order book?
qa_highlights.answer: The approval covers only the current fiscal year and is purely anticipatory; order books are built 2-3 months ahead.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 14% distribution growth, and can it return to 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the slowdown reflects a higher base and parts availability issues. It believes distribution can grow 20% over this year and the next few years, helped by penetration, retrofits and service contracts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data-centre share of power gen, and what is the segment mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Data centres were 40% of Q1 FY27 power gen revenue, up from 23% in Q1 FY26. Power gen split: LHP INR77 crore, MHP INR248 crore, HD INR125 crore; industrial split: construction INR148 crore, rail INR145 crore, compressor INR52 crore, marine INR50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise sharply with flat headcount?
qa_highlights.answer: Three factors: the April 1, 2026 merit increase, a Q1 true-up of variable pay, and an actuarial credit booked in the prior quarter that lowered last quarter's cost.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery depends on whether the Q2 price increase is absorbed and on commodity and freight trends; management gave no margin target.
Export weakness from the Middle East (West Asia crisis) and LHP export decline of 20% YoY.
Distribution growth slowed to 14% in Q1; watch whether it returns toward the 20% level management cites.
High-HP capacity constraints and rising data-centre concentration (40% of power gen revenue) could limit growth or raise concentration risk.
Management succession: the MD said the parent is looking for a successor.
Higher related-party dealings with CTIL and the parent; management says the approvals are only for the current year and that scale drives the choice of entity.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the data-centre pipeline, but cautious and at times evasive on margins, pricing outcomes, exports and the medium-term outlook, citing unprecedented commodity and geopolitical conditions. Management declined to share price-hike size, market share, segment margins and capacity plans beyond current nodes.
key_quotes: Demand is outpacing supply for everyone.
I will not be able to say whether we will hit historic highs or not, because these are unprecedented times in terms of commodity increases and inflation coming at the same time.
This is purely in anticipation, Jonas, just as a prudent governance practice and order books don't get built this early in the year.

growth.why: No explicit numeric revenue guidance; management cites strong end-market demand (data centres ~40% of power gen sales, order velocity) and one price hike at start of Q2 FY27, but no specific new capacity is being added and capex is held in existing plants at 70-75% utilisation.
